content: This document does not include all potential drug interactions. It is essential to maintain a comprehensive list of all products you are using, including prescription medications, over-the-counter drugs, and herbal supplements. Share this list with your healthcare provider and pharmacist to ensure safe and effective treatment. Magnesium has the potential to bind with certain medications, which can interfere with their complete absorption. If you are taking a tetracycline-class antibiotic (such as demeclocycline, doxycycline, minocycline, or tetracycline), ensure that you separate the timing of the magnesium supplement dose from the antibiotic dose by at least 2 to 3 hours. Carefully review the labels of all your prescription, over-the-counter, and herbal products (such as antacids, laxatives, and vitamins) to check for magnesium content, as this may affect your overall magnesium intake. In the event of an overdose, if the individual exhibits severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, immediately call emergency services (911 in the U.S.). For less severe cases, contact a poison control center without delay. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. While taking this medication, it is important to undergo regular laboratory and/or medical tests, such as monitoring magnesium blood levels and kidney function, to ensure safety and efficacy. Attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments as directed by your healthcare provider. Magnesium supplements are available in various forms, each containing different amounts of magnesium. Many of these supplements can be purchased without a prescription. To support your overall health, maintain a well-balanced diet. If you miss a dose of this medication, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time of your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and proceed with your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to make up for the missed one. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Avoid storing it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly dispose of this product when it is expired or no longer needed, following local disposal regulations. This information was last revised in May 2024. It is important to note that this document provides a summary and does not contain all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for your specific situation. This information is not a substitute for individualized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
